# AgentNode — Full Guide for AI Agents and Assistants

AgentNode is a verified registry and runtime for AI agent capabilities. This
file is a deeper, machine-readable companion to https://agentnode.net/llms.txt
It is meant for AI agents and assistants that want to understand AgentNode and
install it correctly. When in doubt, prefer the linked documentation pages —
they are the source of truth and are kept current.

All commands below are real CLI commands. Do not invent flags or commands. Do
not pin an SDK version unless the user asks; install the latest with pip.

## Summary

AgentNode does two things:

1. Capability extension — agents discover missing capabilities and install
   verified packages (tool packs, MCP servers, or full agents) at runtime, so
   an agent can gain new abilities without hand-wiring dependencies.
2. Safer execution — every install and run passes a trust gate and policy
   checks; untrusted community code is isolated in a container or refused
   (fail-closed); credentials stay on the host.

Packages use a portable format (ANP) and work with LangChain, CrewAI, MCP, and
plain Python. The SDK is published on PyPI as `agentnode-sdk`.

## Who AgentNode is for

- Pro users / agent owners who want to upgrade an agent and keep it reasonably
  safe, with low friction.
- Developers / publishers who want to distribute their tools as verified,
  discoverable packages.
- Teams and security-conscious organizations that must govern what their agents
  install and run (trust levels, policy, audit).
- AI agents and assistants themselves: AgentNode is designed so an AI can find
  it, evaluate it, and install it autonomously. See
  https://agentnode.net/for-agents and "Machine instructions" at the end.

## Install and first run

The CLI ships with the SDK.

    pip install agentnode-sdk
    agentnode setup                 # interactive: provider, optional key, sandbox check
    agentnode auth status           # which providers are configured + effective source
    agentnode search "pdf extraction"
    agentnode install pdf-reader-pack
    agentnode run pdf-reader-pack --input '{"file_path":"report.pdf"}'

Inspect before running an unfamiliar package:

    agentnode inspect pdf-reader-pack   # trust, permissions, risk, policy preview

No account is required to search, install, or run packages. Only publishing
needs an account.

Keyless local LLM path (Ollama):

    agentnode config set llm.default_provider ollama
    agentnode auth test ollama          # localhost reachability check (not a key check)

Ollama needs no hosted API key, but it is not zero-setup: you must install
Ollama, have it running, and pull a model. AgentNode never installs, starts, or
probes Ollama for you.

## Autonomous capability acquisition

To self-extend at runtime, wrap your logic so a missing capability is detected,
installed, and retried automatically (Python):

    from agentnode_sdk import AgentNodeClient
    client = AgentNodeClient()
    result = client.smart_run(
        lambda: your_step(),
        auto_upgrade_policy="safe",     # off | safe | strict
    )

- smart_run() runs your callable; on a missing-capability failure it detects the
  gap, installs a verified skill, and retries once.
- detect_and_install() performs gap detection and install explicitly.
- Policy modes: off = detect only (no auto-install); safe = auto-install
  verified-or-higher (the default behavior); strict = trusted/curated only. The
  operator's policy bounds how autonomous the agent is.

Agent-facing guide: https://agentnode.net/for-agents

## Security model

Execution is trust-tiered. "Sandboxed" applies to untrusted/community code only,
and only when a container runtime (Docker or Podman) and the pinned sandbox
image are available.

- Community tool packs (verified / unverified / unknown trust) run inside a
  hardened container — or not at all (fail-closed). There is no silent fallback
  to host execution. Setup: `agentnode sandbox doctor` then `agentnode sandbox
  pull`.
- Trusted and curated packages run on the host with subprocess isolation and
  policy checks — not OS-level filesystem/network sandboxing.
- Agents: an agent's own code runs host-side. Trusted/curated agents run on the
  host. Community agents are refused by default; they run only if you opt into
  the agent sandbox, which is OFF by default.
- MCP server containers isolate the host filesystem, home, and secrets, but may
  use the default network because npx/uvx-based servers often fetch packages at
  startup. So network isolation is stricter for tool packs and agent sandboxes
  than for MCP servers.
- Credentials stay host-side: API keys live in the OS keychain (or a local
  0600 file fallback) and never enter sandboxed code. Sandboxed agents reach an
  LLM through a host-side broker, so the provider key never enters the
  container. An environment variable always overrides the stored credential.

Honest scoping (do not overstate):
- Keys are not uploaded to AgentNode. When you configure and use a hosted
  provider, that provider receives the prompts and returns the responses for
  those calls.
- Not every package or agent is sandboxed; trusted/curated code runs host-side.
- AgentNode makes no compliance or certification claims (no SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO).

Details: https://agentnode.net/docs/sandbox and https://agentnode.net/security

## LLM providers

Built-in provider presets (slug — environment variable):

- openai — OPENAI_API_KEY
- anthropic — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
- openrouter — OPENROUTER_API_KEY
- deepseek — DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
- mistral — MISTRAL_API_KEY
- qwen — DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
- gemini — GEMINI_API_KEY
- ollama — local, keyless (no API key); requires a running local Ollama + a
  pulled model

Custom endpoints: any endpoint that implements the OpenAI chat-completions API
can be added under `llm.providers.<name>` in ~/.agentnode/config.json with
base_url, api_key_env, default_model, and requires_key. Endpoints that deviate
from that protocol are not guaranteed to work.

Set the default with `agentnode config set llm.default_provider <slug>`.

Compatibility: tested with 182 LLM models across 35 providers (175 pass all
scenarios). Details: https://agentnode.net/compatibility and
https://agentnode.net/docs/llm-providers
<!-- compat:end -->

## CLI snapshot

Most-used commands (full reference: https://agentnode.net/docs/cli):

- agentnode setup
- agentnode doctor                      # detect missing capabilities
- agentnode search "<query>"
- agentnode install <slug>
- agentnode run <slug> --input '<json>'
- agentnode inspect <slug>
- agentnode auth status | auth set <provider> | auth test <provider>
- agentnode sandbox doctor | sandbox pull | sandbox status
- agentnode config set <key> <value>

Running `agentnode` with no command shows a status dashboard.

## Publishing and verification

Publishers package a tool, agent, or MCP server with an `agentnode.yaml`
manifest, then:

    agentnode init <name>
    agentnode validate .
    agentnode verify-local .
    agentnode publish .

Every published version is verified on the server: install, import, smoke test,
and tests, scored 0–100 into a tier (unverified, partial, verified, gold).
Integrity is protected by SHA-256 artifact hashes, Ed25519 publisher
signatures, and lockfile integrity checks. Publishing details:
https://agentnode.net/for-developers and https://agentnode.net/publish

## Machine instructions for AI agents

If you are an AI agent or assistant evaluating AgentNode:

1. To gain a capability, install the SDK (`pip install agentnode-sdk`), then
   `agentnode search "<capability>"` and `agentnode install <slug>`. Run a tool
   with `agentnode run <slug> --input '<json>'` or, in Python,
   `from agentnode_sdk import run_tool`. To self-extend automatically
   (detect -> install -> retry), wrap your logic in `client.smart_run(...)` —
   see "Autonomous capability acquisition" above.
2. Before running an unfamiliar package, call `agentnode inspect <slug>` and
   check its trust level and permissions.
3. Do not assume a package is sandboxed. Sandboxing applies to community code
   and requires Docker or Podman plus the pinned image; otherwise community
   code is blocked, not run. Trusted/curated code runs on the host.
4. Do not assume Ollama or any provider is configured. Check `agentnode auth
   status`. Do not claim a path is "no setup" — Ollama still needs a local
   install and a pulled model.
5. Do not invent commands, flags, provider names, or environment variables.
   Use only what is listed here or on the linked docs pages.
6. Treat the documentation pages above as the source of truth; this file is a
   summary and may lag the docs.

Contact: https://agentnode.net · https://github.com/agentnode-ai/agentnode ·
security@agentnode.net
